# Kyoto 4-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A relaxed Kyoto itinerary centered on temples, food markets, and one easy nature outing, with daily walking kept moderate and one rainy-day backup built into each day. I’m assuming a mid-range hotel near Kyoto Station or a major rail hub, public transit between sights, and one vegetarian traveler needing reliable meal options.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget

| Day | Focus | Plan | Est. Steps | Est. Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Day 1 — Apr 10 | Kyoto Station area + Gion | Arrive, check in, light temple walk, evening food lane | 8,000–10,000 | $320 |
| Day 2 — Apr 11 | Higashiyama temples | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, Pontocho dinner | 11,000–13,500 | $340 |
| Day 3 — Apr 12 | Arashiyama nature day | Bamboo grove, river area, easy scenic walk, temple stop | 10,000–13,000 | $420 |
| Day 4 — Apr 13 | Nishiki Market + central Kyoto | Market breakfast, downtown temples, departure buffer | 7,000–9,500 | $250 |

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Easy Arrival, Gion Evening, and Station-Side Dining
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive in Kyoto, store luggage if needed, and check in near **Kyoto Station** or **Karasuma** for easy transit.
- **Afternoon:** Keep it light with **Higashi Hongan-ji** or a short walk around the station area; both are low-effort first-day choices.
- **Dinner:** Go to **Gion** or **Nishiki nearby** for tofu, yuba, soba, or tempura; one traveler can stay fully vegetarian without difficulty.
- **Rainy backup:** Kyoto Station indoor areas, **Kyoto Tower**, or **Kyoto Railway Museum** for a low-walking first day.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170, transit $10, meals $80, admissions/snacks $20, buffer $40 = **$320**

### Day 2: Higashiyama Temples, Historic Streets, and Evening Food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Start at **Kiyomizu-dera** early to avoid crowds and keep the pace comfortable.
- **Afternoon:** Walk downhill through **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka**, then continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and nearby lanes.
- **Dinner:** Choose **Pontocho** or a central vegan-friendly restaurant for set meals, noodles, or tofu cuisine.
- **Rainy backup:** **Kyoto National Museum** or **Kyoto City Kyocera Museum of Art**.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170, transit $10, admissions $20, meals $90, snacks/taxis $50 = **$340**

### Day 3: Relaxed Arashiyama Nature Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Arashiyama** early for the bamboo grove and river area before it gets busy.
- **Afternoon:** Keep the nature activity relaxed with a gentle stroll by the **Katsura River** and one temple stop such as **Tenryu-ji**.
- **Dinner:** Return to central Kyoto for a quieter dinner; look for vegetarian curry, soba, or tofu kaiseki.
- **Rainy backup:** **Arashiyama Monkey Park** is less ideal in heavy rain, so use **Kyoto Aquarium** or **Randen line sightseeing** instead.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170, transit $12, admissions $25, meals $95, optional boat/extra activity $118 = **$420**

### Day 4: Nishiki Market, Central Kyoto Temples, Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Nishiki Market** for breakfast and snack shopping; this is the best day for food-focused browsing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Visit **Nishiki Market** for breakfast and snack shopping; this is the best day for food-focused browsing, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Fit in a short temple stop such as **Nijo Castle** or **Shosei-en Garden** depending on departure time.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/64/Gate%2C_Sh%C5%8Dsei-en%2C_Kyoto_-_Apr_3%2C_2013.jpg Alt=Afternoon:** Fit in a short temple stop such as **Nijo Castle** or **Shosei-en Garden** depending on departure time, Kyoto, Japan
- **Dinner:** If flying out late, have an early final meal near Kyoto Station; otherwise use the budget for a transfer and takeaway snacks.
- **Rainy backup:** Spend extra time in **Nishiki Market covered arcades** and nearby department store food halls.
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170, transit $10, meals $60, admissions $10, luggage/storage/taxis $0 = **$250**

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

- **Hotel:** about **$680** total for 4 nights
- **Food:** about **$325**
- **Transit:** about **$42**
- **Admissions and activities:** about **$75**
- **Rainy-day extras / taxi buffer:** about **$200**
- **Trip total:** about **$1,322**

This stays well under your **$2,400** cap, leaving room for a nicer hotel, more sit-down meals, or a special dinner.

## Stay, Food, and Pace Notes

- **Best hotel area:** **Kyoto Station** is the safest choice for your constraints because it minimizes transfers and makes rainy-day changes easy.
- **Step target:** This plan stays mostly around **7,000–13,500 steps/day**, below your 14,000-step limit.
- **Vegetarian-friendly dining:** Kyoto is strong for **tofu, yuba, soba, tempura, curry, and vegan ramen**; restaurants near **Gion, Kyoto Station, and central Kyoto** are easiest.
- **Best transport:** Use **subway, buses sparingly, and taxis only when needed** to protect the walking limit.
